name: Titan Company Ltd
about: Titan Company Ltd is among India’s most respected lifestyle companies. It has established leadership positions in the Watches, Jewellery and Eyewear categories led by its trusted brands and differentiated customer experience. It was founded in 1984 as a joint-venture between TATA Group and Tamilnadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO). [1]

sections.one_liner: Titan is India's largest branded jeweller; Q1 FY27's 14% margin was flattered by one-offs, while debt has tripled.
business: Lifestyle retailer with 3,603 stores across 440+ towns: jewellery, watches, eyecare, fragrances, bags, ethnic wear and engineering (TEAL). [AR FY26]
Jewellery brands are Tanishq, Zoya, Mia, CaratLane and Damas; 67% of Damas was acquired in Q3 FY26 and consolidated from 1 January 2026. [Q3FY26 call]
Segment revenue shares and geographic mix are not disclosed in the material; jewellery clearly dominates the narrative and the economics. [AR FY26]
49m Encircle loyalty members. Exchange is part of over 50% of jewellery sales, and purchase plans make up 20-25% of the business. [AR FY26][Q3FY26 call]
financial_snapshot: Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026): revenue ₹21,356cr, up 29.3% YoY; EBITDA ₹2,890cr at 14% margin; PAT ₹1,777cr, up 62.9%. [Numbers]
Removing ₹407cr customs gain gives roughly 11.6% EBITDA margin. Also removing 75-80bps inventory revaluation gain gives about 10.8%, near the trend line. [Numbers][Q1FY27 call]
Trailing 12 months: revenue ₹92,417cr, EBITDA ₹9,416cr (10.2%), PAT ₹5,760cr. FY26 return on capital 21% versus 25% peak in FY23. [Numbers]
Valuation: P/E 67.7x, price/book about 25x (₹4,448 vs ₹177 book). Return on equity of 37.7% is boosted by debt-to-equity of 1.95. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue compound annual growth is 29.2% over 3 years and 32.3% over 5 years. FY26 revenue rose 44.9% to ₹87,584cr, partly from consolidating Damas. [Numbers]
PAT 3-year growth is only 15.7%, against 29.2% for revenue. Operating margin fell from 12% (FY22-23) to 9-10% (FY24-26). [Numbers]
Return on capital fell from 25% (FY23) to 19% (FY25), then recovered to 21% (FY26). Scale is growing faster than returns. [Numbers]
Jewellery buyers grew -2% (Q2 FY26), 8% (Q4) and 5% (Q1 FY27), versus 24-80% revenue growth. Growth comes mostly from gold price and ticket size. [Q2FY26/Q4FY26/Q1FY27 calls][Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings rose 3.3x, from ₹9,367cr (FY23) to ₹30,621cr (FY26). Debt-to-equity rose from 0.79 to 1.95 and has increased every year. [Numbers]
Net worth fell from ₹11,851cr to ₹9,393cr in FY24 despite ₹3,496cr profit. The reason is not disclosed. [Numbers]
Inventory is 222 days and the cash cycle 211 days, yet working-capital days are only 28. This implies most inventory is funded by liabilities, likely including gold loans. [Numbers]
cash_quality: Over FY24-26, operating cash flow was ₹6,744cr against ₹11,906cr PAT, a ratio of 0.57. Reported profit converts to cash only partly. [Numbers]
Free cash flow swung from -₹1,011cr (FY25) to ₹4,713cr (FY26). Three-year cumulative free cash flow is only ₹4,726cr. [Numbers]
Borrowings rose ₹15,093cr over FY25-26 while free cash flow added ₹3,702cr. Growth, Damas and inventory are debt-funded; the Damas price is not disclosed. [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: Agree: management prioritises absolute profit over margin %. Numbers confirm it: PAT grew 15.7% a year over 3 years versus 29.2% revenue growth, and margin fell 2pts. [Q2FY26 call][Numbers]
Diverge: Q4 FY26 topline called 'superlative' (+80.5% YoY), but margin was 7% and EBITDA fell 29% quarter-on-quarter. The cause is not disclosed. [Q4FY26 call][Numbers]
Diverge: management says strong balance sheets favour organised players, yet Titan's debt-to-equity rose from 0.79 to 1.95 in three years. [Q4FY26 call][Numbers]
Q1 FY27 'all-round growth' rests partly on one-offs. The ₹407cr customs gain alone equals about 1.9pts of revenue, and management says these gains reverse in Q2-Q3. [Q1FY27 call][Numbers]
guidance: Jewellery EBIT margin centred on 11%, give or take, for FY27; Q1 underlying margin was 10.9%. [Q1FY27 call]
Jewellery growth of 15-20% a year over 3-5 years; no specific FY27 number given. [Q4FY26 call]
CaratLane margin moving toward 10%; TEAL normalised margin toward 12-16% over the long term. [Q1FY27 call]
International business positive for full-year FY27. Non-Damas operations earn 5-6% EBIT, while Damas Core is loss-making because of the war. [Q1FY27 call]
Customs gains to be realised in Q2 and Q3 FY27 as inventory sells; full-year impact not quantified. [Q1FY27 call]

ledger.promised: Jewellery growth in H2 better than H1. [Q2FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Group revenue growth: H1 24.6%/28.8%, H2 43.3%/80.5%; jewellery grew 40% in Q3.

ledger.promised: Eyewear division to close FY26 at 13-14% growth. [Q2FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: EyeCare growing 16-17% year-on-year per Q4 call; segment figures not in NUMBERS.

ledger.promised: Jewellery EBIT to grow slightly slower than revenue. [Q2FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Segment EBIT not disclosed. Group EBITDA +46.8% vs revenue +44.9% suggests otherwise.
Mar-26 revenue ₹26,920cr, +80.5% YoY and +5.9% QoQ, consistent with consolidation.

ledger.promised: Jewellery margins pressured if gold stays elevated. [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Mar-26 margin 7% vs 10% a year earlier; Damas mix effect not separated out.

ledger.promised: Very positive on Damas and international over the next 2-3 quarters. [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Q1 FY27: Damas Core loss-making from war; other international at 5-6% EBIT.

ledger.promised: Jewellery EBIT margin centred on 11%. [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: Q1 underlying 10.9%; reported group margin 14% includes one-offs. Sep-26 quarter not reported.

ledger.promised: Customs/inventory revaluation gains realised and reversed through Q2-Q3. [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: Sep-26 quarter not yet in NUMBERS.

bull: Revenue compound growth of 32.3% over 5 years and return on capital of 21% at ₹87,584cr scale; market share gained 50-60bps in FY26. [Numbers][Q4FY26 call]
FY26 operating cash flow ₹5,590cr, 1.10x PAT, after a negative FY25. Free cash flow ₹4,713cr shows the cash engine works when inventory stabilises. [Numbers]
Underlying Q1 FY27 PAT growth stays strong even after removing the ₹407cr customs gain. Studded jewellery recovery supports H2 mix. [Numbers][Q1FY27 call]
bear: At 67.7x earnings, PAT has grown 15.7% a year over 3 years; margins fell from 12% to 10%. Competitive discounting shows 'no easing'. [Numbers][Q1FY27 call]
Debt-to-equity of 1.95 and 222 inventory days leave Titan exposed to gold-price swings. Operating cash covered only 57% of PAT over 3 years. [Numbers]
The 14% Q1 margin includes about 2.6pts of one-offs that reverse in Q2-Q3. Damas is loss-making, and the acquisition's returns are not disclosed. [Q1FY27 call][Numbers]
questions: What drove the Q4 FY26 margin of 7%: Damas, gold costs, or discounting?
What did Damas cost, and what is its loss in Q1 FY27?
What borrowing level and debt-to-equity ratio do you consider the ceiling?
What is Q1 FY27 PAT excluding customs and inventory revaluation gains?

analyst_pushback.question: Does CaratLane Q4 slowdown suggest fungibility between gold and studded jewelry?
analyst_pushback.response: No. Slowdown was internal ERP migration issue (Oracle Fusion). December and April data show this was a blip.

analyst_pushback.question: What is beYon market acceptance versus CaratLane/Mia?
analyst_pushback.response: Sample size of one store too small. Good traction in Valentine's but need more stores for rigorous assessment.

annual_report.business: Titan is India's leading lifestyle company founded in 1984 (Tata Group & TIDCO). Operates across jewellery, watches, eyewear, fragrances, women's bags and Indian dress wear through 3,603 stores. Revenue-driven by premium and mid-market consumer aspirations through branded retail.

segments.name: Jewellery
segments.comment: Tanishq, Zoya, Gold Plus, Mia, CaratLane, Taneira, Damas

segments.name: Fragrances & Women's Bags
segments.comment: SKINN premium fine fragrance, IRTH handbags

annual_report.revenue_mix: Domestic multi-brand portfolio across 440+ towns in India. 49 million Encircle Members. No geographic or product-level breakdown stated in opening pages.
strategy: Combine design with engineering across categories
Expand presence in untapped towns and formats
Drive innovation in products and retail experiences
Build consumer relationships through loyalty programs
Integrate Tata Group values: purpose, excellence, corporate citizenship
annual_report.outlook: Management aims to scale frontiers by exploring new possibilities across categories and markets. Focus on distinctive offerings, seamless experiences and community contributions as consumer aspirations evolve.
